search_strategy: Chat: the agent first used Mattermost's server-side full-text search API (/teams/{id}/posts/search) with a curated 8-term list (ledger, seed, next_speaker, sentinel, interleave, sidecar, desync, turn) -- strong for anything containing the technical vocabulary but blind to plain-English remarks (e.g. 'negotiation demo', 'whose turn it was', 'trailing period'). It then dumped EVERY channel in full (code-review 3243 lines, engineering 2501, pipeline 2009, releases 665, cookbooks 774, viewer 312, incidents 243, general/help/random/off-topic/town-square) and grepped the dumps with a rotating set of technical-keyword patterns (sidecar/ledger/next_speaker/interleave/SENTINEL; write_sidecar/read_sidecar/verify_sidecar/TURN_LEDGER_VERSION/186/189; SENTINEL/marker/<<END/END_OF/DONE; version/trim/cut it back/source of truth; num_cached/cached/adopt) rather than reading full channels sequentially -- #releases was dumped but never grepped or read at all, and #viewer/#cookbooks got only narrow keyword passes plus two short wide sed ranges. This is why every miss in #releases, #viewer and most of #cookbooks/#code-review/#engineering is a genuinely plain-worded remark that no keyword pattern happened to catch, not a truncation problem. Mail: read over raw IMAP (imaplib), first with a 9-term TEXT search (ledger, turn_ledger, next_speaker, seed, interleave, COMPLETION_SENTINEL, adopt_ledger, multi-turn, 'turn ledger') that returned 0 hits for 4 of 9 terms, then a narrower 3-term sweep (ledger, interleave, resume) that pulled 43 full messages into one file and was read in full via sed ranges -- both searches are r1-biased; neither ever searched for marker/sentinel/stop/AttributeError, so the two r2 mail threads (g7r2-l05, g7r2-l08) were never fetched at all. Wiki: excellent technique where used -- the agent knew from the ticket's own hint that BookStack search does not index comments, used /api/pages/{id} to pull body+comments together, and was the FIRST source it opened (pages 143, 144, 139 fetched at steps 14-18, well before chat/mail). It also caught and worked around a duplicate-book problem (every wiki page exists twice, under two book ids) by enumerating /api/pages?count=500 in full.
